name: Temne
notes: Temne, Mel branch of Atlantic-Congo (not close to Mande, despite sharing Sierra Leone with Mende), spoken by ~2 million people mainly in Northern Sierra Leone and the Western Area. Nine vowel qualities /i e ɛ ə a ʌ o ɔ u/ are attested; the back vowel ⟨ʌ⟩ has an ASCII-safe variant ⟨ȧ⟩ in texts without extended-Latin support, not modelled separately here. Temne unusually distinguishes DENTAL ⟨th⟩ /t̪/ from ALVEOLAR ⟨t⟩ /t/ (with articulatory roles reversed from the cross-linguistic norm: the dental is apical, the alveolar laminal — a fact about articulation, not spelling, and not otherwise relevant to the grapheme map). Labiovelar stops are written ⟨gb⟩ /ɡb/ and ⟨kp⟩ /kp/, as in the neighbouring but unrelated Mende (men) and Susu (sus). Temne is a two-tone (high/low) language; tone is not marked in the standard Latin orthography, so no tone is emitted here. Quality:research — the alphabet table (27 letters/digraphs) is reconstructed from a secondary Wikipedia summary that did not give every letter explicitly; the affricate /tʃ/ attested in the consonant inventory is not assigned a grapheme here because no source consulted states its orthographic letter unambiguously (candidate ⟨ch⟩ is a plausible West African convention but unconfirmed for Temne specifically, so it is omitted rather than guessed, per AGENTS.md §4).
